title: Design private audit routing and customer-managed sink patterns
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Define robust, auditable, and operator-friendly patterns for forwarding audit logs from Private / VPC / on-prem Redwood deployments into customer-managed storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob or on-prem object stores). Goals include: end-to-end integrity, tenant isolation, minimal operator burden, clear RBAC/SSO control points for enabling forwarding, support for air-gapped import bundles, and operational observability and metrics. Constraints: customers require control over their storage keys and retention; some deployments are air-gapped; we must avoid uploading raw plaintext sensitive debug payloads; throughput can vary by tenant and we must support graceful backpressure and retry semantics.
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — scoped supported sink types: S3 (v2/v4), GCS, Azure Blob, generic S3-compatible endpoints (MinIO). Agreed to design for both push (Redwood → customer) and pull (customer pulls manifests) modes.

2026-03-11: Threat modeling session — added HMAC-signed manifest and upload-level checksums to prevent tampering; decided to default to TLS mutual auth for dedicated/private setups that can accept TLS client certs.

2026-03-12: Design spike — prototyped multipart commit protocol: chunked uploads with per-chunk checksums, a final manifest.json with sequence numbers and HMAC signed by server private key for integrity. This enables idempotent resume and watermarking.

2026-03-12: Trade-offs — opted NOT to require customer KMS integration for uploads in hosted-managed flows to simplify onboarding; for Private/VPC flows we will support customer-managed CMEK/TLS handshakes and envelope encryption using customer KMS via a negotiated handshake documented in the design link.

2026-03-13: RBAC and admin controls — RBAC v2 roles defined: audit.forward.config (can configure sinks), audit.forward.admin (can rotate sink credentials), audit.forward.view (can view status). Admin UI changes planned: explicit SSO/SAML approval flow when enabling forwarding; SSO group mapping to RBAC roles for enterprise customers.

2026-03-13: Review feedback from Security — require retention enforcement metadata to be embedded in manifests to prevent accidental deletion; require per-tenant upload quotas and rate-limiting recommendations for customer buckets.

2026-03-14: Infra feedback — added requirement for backpressure signals: 413 responses from customer endpoints should trigger exponential backoff and a local durable queue with configurable maximum retention; metrics: per-tenant failed-chunk-rate, upload-latency histogram, and manifest-commit-failures counter.

acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Infra
Prototype connector that uploads to an S3-compatible endpoint with multipart chunking and signed manifest
RBAC v2 roles and admin UI wireframes completed and validated with PM/Design
End-to-end tests for resume/idempotency and envelope encryption (CMEK) in private deployment mode
Observability dashboard with per-tenant metrics and alert thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for checksum and HMAC manifest verification
Integration tests against S3/GCS/Azure test clusters including auth variations (IAM, presigned URLs, SAS tokens)
Airgap import test: generate signed bundle, import to air-gapped cluster, verify manifest and replayability
Chaos test: simulate intermittent 5xx from customer endpoint and verify backoff and local queue behavior
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood in staging with Redwood-managed customer buckets (low impact)
Phase 1: Beta with 3 enterprise customers in private/VPC deployments with CMEK enabled
Phase 2: General availability for Dedicated and Private; gated by completed security review and compliance sign-off
notes_on_rbac_and_admin_controls: RBAC v2 integration: new permissions audit.forward.{config,admin,view} enforced in control plane UI and API; enabling forwarding requires audit.forward.config and a signed admin approval via SSO SAML assertion for enterprise orgs
SSO/SAML considerations: when a tenant grants forwarding, the SSO assertion will be used to map the operator to the appropriate RBAC role; audit trail records who configured sink and when
UI guardrails: show live validation of sink credentials and retention policy warnings; prevent non-admins from rotating sink credentials or supplying CMEK keys
Admin audit events: configuration.create, configuration.update, configuration.rotate-credentials emitted to local audit log and included in manifest metadata for cross-checking
incident_learnings: INC-2025-09-audit-drop: during a major outage we observed lost audit events because the forwarder accepted 200 from a malformed proxy. Mitigation: manifest-level sequence numbers and verification to detect missing blocks.
INC-2025-12-slow-upload: large tenants caused head-of-line blocking — mitigation: per-tenant upload worker pool and adaptive chunk size.
